decks.title: Tissues — Part 1: Plant tissues
goals: Classify meristems as apical, intercalary and lateral and say where each is found
Compare parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma in structure and function
State the components and functions of xylem and phloem

slides.heading: Tissues
slides.body_md: Part 1 — how plants divide the work: growing tissues and permanent tissues.

visual.alt: Flow splitting plant tissues into meristematic tissue that divides and permanent tissue that is specialised

slides.narration: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to do one job. In a plant some tissues keep dividing so that the plant grows. Others have stopped dividing and have settled into a particular job.

slides.heading: Where the meristems lie
slides.body_md: **Meristems** are tissues whose cells keep dividing. They are **apical**, **intercalary** or **lateral**.

slides.narration: Look at where growth happens. The tips of the shoot and the root hold the apical meristems. At the base of an internode lies the intercalary meristem. And along the stem a thin layer called the cambium forms the lateral meristem.

slides.heading: Three kinds of meristem

rows: Base of leaves or internodes, as in grasses
Along the sides of stems and roots (cambium)

visual.alt: Table of apical, intercalary and lateral meristems with position and effect

slides.narration: Apical and intercalary meristems lengthen the plant. The lateral meristem makes stems and roots thicker. Meristematic cells are small, have thin walls, dense cytoplasm and a large nucleus, and have no big vacuole.

slides.heading: Quick check: increasing length
slides.body_md: Which meristem is found at the tip of a root?
slides.narration: The name tells you the position.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: which meristem is at work?
slides.body_md: A gardener marks a bean shoot tip. It grows 2 cm a day. How much longer is it after 14 days, and which meristem is responsible?
bullets: Step 1: growth is **2 cm** a day for **14 days**.
Step 3: growth in **length** at a **tip** is due to the **apical meristem**.

rows: Growth is at the shoot tip

visual.alt: Worked table linking each clue about the shoot to the apical meristem and the total growth

slides.narration: First work out the length gained by multiplying the daily growth by the number of days. Then name the meristem. Growth in length at a tip is the work of the apical meristem.

slides.heading: Simple permanent tissues
slides.body_md: In **simple permanent tissues** all the cells are alike: **parenchyma**, **collenchyma** and **sclerenchyma**.

slides.narration: Parenchyma cells are thin walled and living, with spaces between them. Collenchyma cells are living too, but their corners are thickened. Sclerenchyma cells are dead with thick, hard walls.

slides.heading: Comparing the simple tissues

rows: Living, thin wall, spaces between cells
Soft parts of stems, roots, leaves, fruits
Living, corners of the wall thickened
Below the epidermis of stems and in leaf stalks
Dead, thick lignified wall, no spaces
Husks, seed coats, fibres of jute

visual.alt: Table comparing parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma on cells, function and where found

slides.narration: Parenchyma stores food. Collenchyma supports parts that must bend, like leaf stalks. Sclerenchyma is the hard, strong tissue, as in the fibres of jute and the shell of a nut.

slides.heading: Quick check: flexible support
slides.body_md: Which tissue gives flexible support to leaf stalks and young stems?
slides.narration: Its cells are living, with thickened corners.

slides.narration: Xylem vessels are wide dead tubes that carry water and minerals upwards. Phloem sieve tubes are living but have no nucleus, and each has a companion cell beside it that does. Phloem carries food in both directions.

slides.heading: Components of xylem and phloem

rows: Tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma
Conducts water and minerals upwards; supports
Sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres, phloem parenchyma
Conducts food from leaves to all parts

visual.alt: Table of the components and functions of xylem and phloem

slides.narration: Each of these tissues is made of several kinds of cell. Xylem has tracheids, vessels, fibres and parenchyma. Phloem has sieve tubes, companion cells, fibres and parenchyma. Only the xylem fibres, tracheids and vessels are dead.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: the stained celery
slides.body_md: A celery stalk stands in red ink. The colour climbs 15 cm in 30 minutes. Which tissue is stained, and how far will the ink rise in two hours at this speed?
bullets: Step 1: the ink moves **up** through narrow dead tubes: **xylem**.
Step 2: speed = 15 cm in 30 minutes = **30 cm an hour**.
Step 3: in two hours: 30 × 2 = **60 cm**.

visual.alt: Worked table: xylem is stained, the ink rises thirty centimetres an hour and sixty centimetres in two hours

slides.narration: The red ink shows the path of water, so the stained strands are xylem. Fifteen centimetres in half an hour is thirty centimetres in a full hour, so in two hours the ink would climb sixty centimetres.

slides.heading: Quick check: carrying food
slides.body_md: Which plant tissue carries food from the leaves to the other parts?
slides.narration: Its sieve tubes are living.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Meristems divide: apical and intercalary lengthen, lateral thickens.
Parenchyma stores, collenchyma flexibly supports, sclerenchyma strengthens.
Xylem: tracheids, vessels, fibres, parenchyma; carries water and minerals.
Phloem: sieve tubes, companion cells, fibres, parenchyma; carries food.

visual.alt: Summary table showing which plant tissues are living and which are dead

slides.narration: To recap. Meristems keep dividing. Parenchyma stores, collenchyma bends and supports, sclerenchyma is hard and dead. Xylem moves water upwards and phloem moves food.

slides.heading: Exam tips
bullets: Say **apical** for length at tips and **lateral** for girth.
Sclerenchyma is **dead**; collenchyma is **living**: do not swap them.
Sieve tubes are **living** but have **no nucleus**; the **companion cell** has it.
Tabulate with **matching points** side by side.
slides.narration: Exam tips. Name apical meristems for length and lateral meristems for thickness. Sclerenchyma is dead and collenchyma is alive. Sieve tubes lack a nucleus, so the companion cell controls them. Write comparisons point against point.

slides.heading: Types of connective tissue

slides.narration: Learn each tissue by where it is and what it does. Tendons join muscle to bone and ligaments join bone to bone. Blood has a fluid matrix called plasma.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: naming the tissue

bullets: Step 1: the cord joins **muscle to bone**.
Step 2: a connective tissue that does this is a **tendon**.
Step 3: it passes the pull of the muscle on to the bone.

visual.alt: Table: tendon joins muscle to bone and ligament joins bone to bone

slides.narration: Ask what the cord joins. Muscle to bone means a tendon. Bone to bone means a ligament. The tendon passes the pull of the muscle to the bone so that the bone moves.

slides.heading: Quick check: storing fat
slides.body_md: Which connective tissue stores fat?
slides.narration: Its cells are large with a fat droplet.

slides.heading: Three kinds of muscle

visual.alt: Table comparing striated, unstriated and cardiac muscle

slides.narration: Compare them in a table. Striated muscle moves the limbs and is voluntary. Unstriated muscle moves food along the gut without our control. Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: a tireless muscle
slides.body_md: A resting heart beats 72 times a minute. How many beats in an hour and in a day? Which muscle is this?
bullets: Step 1: 72 × 60 = **4320 beats** in an hour.
Step 2: 4320 × 24 = **103680 beats** in a day.
Step 3: the muscle of the heart is **cardiac muscle**, which does not tire.

visual.alt: Worked table of heartbeats in a minute, an hour and a day

slides.narration: Multiply step by step. Seventy two beats in each minute gives four thousand three hundred and twenty in an hour. Multiply by twenty four hours for the whole day. Only cardiac muscle can keep this up.

slides.body_md: Which muscle is striated but involuntary?
slides.narration: Think of the muscle of the heart.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Epithelium: squamous, cuboidal, columnar, ciliated.
Connective: areolar, adipose, cartilage, bone, tendon, ligament, blood.
Muscle: striated (voluntary), unstriated and cardiac (involuntary).
Nervous tissue: neurons carry impulses.

slides.narration: To recap. Epithelium covers and lines. Connective tissue binds, supports and transports. Muscle moves the body and its organs. Nervous tissue carries impulses so that the parts of the body work together.

slides.heading: Exam tips
bullets: **Tendon**: muscle to bone. **Ligament**: bone to bone.
**Cardiac** muscle is **striated** yet **involuntary**.
In a neuron diagram label **dendrites**, **cell body**, **nucleus**, **axon**, **axon terminals**.
Give **location and function** together when asked to identify a tissue.
slides.narration: Exam tips. Do not swap tendons and ligaments. Remember that cardiac muscle is striped but involuntary. When you draw a neuron, label the dendrites, cell body, nucleus, axon and terminals. And always give the location along with the function.

notes.title: Tissues — Notes

sections.heading: 1. Plant tissues: meristematic tissues
sections.body_md:
A **tissue** is a group of similar cells with a common origin that perform a particular function. Plant tissues are of two groups: **meristematic** (dividing) and **permanent** (specialised, not dividing).

**Features of meristematic cells:** small, thin-walled, closely packed with **no intercellular spaces**, dense cytoplasm, a large nucleus and no (or very small) vacuoles; they divide actively.

| Meristem | Position | Function |
|---|---|---|
| **Apical** | Tips of roots and shoots | Increases **length** |
| **Intercalary** | Base of leaves or internodes (as in grasses) | Increases length at the nodes |
| **Lateral** | Along the sides of stems and roots (**cambium**) | Increases **girth** (thickness) |

key_terms.definition_md: A group of similar cells that do one job together.
The lateral meristem that thickens stems and roots.

sections.heading: 2. Plant tissues: permanent tissues
sections.body_md:
**Simple permanent tissues** (all cells alike):
- **Parenchyma:** **living**, thin cellulose walls, **intercellular spaces**; **stores** food, and in green parts (**chlorenchyma**) makes food by photosynthesis; air-filled parenchyma in aquatic plants (aerenchyma) gives buoyancy.
- **Collenchyma:** **living**, walls **unevenly thickened at the corners** with cellulose and pectin; gives **flexible support** to young stems and leaf stalks.
- **Sclerenchyma:** **dead**, very thick **lignified** walls, narrow cavity, no spaces; gives **strength and hardness**. **Fibres** (jute, coconut husk) are long; **sclereids** (stone cells in guava, nut shells) are short.

**Complex permanent tissues** (several kinds of cell working together):
- **Xylem:** **tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma**. Conducts **water and minerals** from roots to leaves (upwards) and gives support. All except the parenchyma are dead.
- **Phloem:** **sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres, phloem parenchyma**. Conducts **food** from the leaves to all parts (up and down). Sieve tubes are **living but have no nucleus**; the **companion cell** has a nucleus and controls them.

key_terms.definition_md: Living thin-walled tissue that stores food.
Living tissue with thickened corners; flexible support.
Tissue that carries water and minerals.

sections.heading: 3. Animal tissues: epithelial and connective
sections.body_md:
**Epithelial tissue** covers the body and lines cavities and tubes. Cells are closely packed with little matrix, resting on a basement layer.
| Type | Where | Function |
|---|---|---|
| **Squamous** | Air sacs of lungs, blood vessels, mouth | Protection; diffusion |
| **Cuboidal** | Kidney tubules, ducts of glands | Secretion, absorption |
| **Columnar** | Stomach and intestine lining | Secretion, absorption |
| **Ciliated** | Windpipe | Moves mucus and dust |
**Glandular epithelium** (goblet cells, salivary glands) secretes.

**Connective tissue** has cells scattered in a **matrix**; it binds, supports and fills.
| Tissue | Where | Function |
|---|---|---|
| **Areolar** | Under the skin, around organs | Binds, fills spaces |
| **Adipose** | Under skin, around kidneys | Stores fat; insulates |
| **Cartilage** | Ear, nose, ends of bones | Flexible support |
| **Bone** | Skeleton | Hard support; protection |
| **Tendon** | Muscle to bone | Strong, inelastic; transmits pull |
| **Ligament** | Bone to bone | Elastic; holds joints |
| **Blood** | Vessels | Transports; fluid matrix **plasma** |

sections.body_md:
| Point | Striated (skeletal) | Unstriated (smooth) | Cardiac |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stripes | Present | Absent | Present |
| Control | Voluntary | Involuntary | Involuntary |
| Cell | Long, cylindrical, unbranched, many nuclei | Spindle-shaped, one nucleus | Branched, usually one nucleus; intercalated discs |
| Found in | Limbs, attached to bones | Walls of gut, blood vessels | Heart |
| Fatigue | Tires | Tires slowly | Does not tire |

**Nervous tissue** is made of **neurons**. A neuron has **dendrites** (receive impulses), a **cell body (cyton)** with a **nucleus**, a long **axon** (carries impulses away, often wrapped in a **myelin sheath**) and **axon terminals** (pass on the impulse). Neurons are the structural and functional units of the nervous system.

sections.heading: 5. Role of tissues in physiological processes
sections.body_md:
Structure fits function:
- **Transport in plants:** xylem (water and minerals up) and phloem (food up and down): long tubes joined end to end.
- **Support:** sclerenchyma (hard dead fibres), collenchyma (flexible), and in animals bone and cartilage.
- **Storage:** parenchyma (starch, water), adipose tissue (fat).
- **Gas exchange:** thin squamous epithelium of the air sacs.
- **Protection:** epithelium of the skin; sclerenchyma husks.
- **Movement:** muscular tissue, whose fibres contract; tendons pass the pull to bones.
- **Coordination:** nervous tissue, whose long branched neurons carry impulses.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Calling sclerenchyma living, or collenchyma dead.
- Saying sieve tubes have a nucleus; it is the companion cell that has one.
- Mixing up tendons (muscle to bone) and ligaments (bone to bone).
- Writing that cardiac muscle is unstriated or voluntary.
- Forgetting the cambium: it is the **lateral** meristem that increases girth.

**How marks are usually awarded**
- 1 mark: a term, a location, an odd one out **with its category**.
- 2 marks: two differences matched point for point; two functions.
- 3 marks: a neat, labelled diagram of a neuron (outline, key features, labels) or three differences in a table.
- 10-mark structured question: a short situation or diagram with parts of 3, 3 and 4 marks; one part is usually a labelled diagram.

questions.stem_md: Which meristem is found at the tip of a root?
questions.solution_md: The tips of roots and shoots hold the apical meristems — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Which tissue gives flexible support to leaf stalks and young stems?
questions.solution_md: Living collenchyma with thickened corners supports parts that bend — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Which plant tissue carries food from the leaves to the other parts of the plant?
questions.solution_md: Sieve tubes of the phloem conduct food — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Which epithelium lines the air sacs of the lungs?
questions.solution_md: Thin flat cells let gases diffuse easily — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Which connective tissue stores fat?
questions.solution_md: Adipose cells are filled with fat — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Which muscle is striated but involuntary?
questions.solution_md: Cardiac muscle is striped but works without our control — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Which feature of a neuron suits it to carry impulses over long distances?
questions.solution_md: The long axon carries the impulse far from the cell body — option (b).

questions.stem_md: A wire loosely tied round a young tree trunk is found years later buried in the wood because the trunk has thickened. The tissue that thickened it is the

options.text_md: apical meristem at the shoot tip

questions.solution_md: The cambium adds new tissue on its sides and increases girth — option (b).

questions.stem_md: After a lawn mower cuts off the tops of grass leaves, the leaves go on lengthening from their bases. The tissue responsible is the
questions.solution_md: Grasses have an intercalary meristem at the base of the leaves and internodes — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Under a microscope a student sees small, closely packed cells with thin walls, dense cytoplasm, a large nucleus, no vacuole and no spaces between them. The tissue is
questions.solution_md: These are features of dividing, meristematic cells — option (d).

questions.stem_md: A shoot tip grows 2 cm every day. How many centimetres does it lengthen in 14 days?
questions.solution_md: $2 \times 14 = 28$ cm.

questions.stem_md: Give the biological term: the lateral meristem that increases the girth of a stem.

answer.model_answer_md: **Cambium.**

questions.solution_md: Cambium.

questions.stem_md: True or false? Meristematic cells have a large central vacuole and thick walls.
questions.solution_md: False. Meristematic cells have thin walls, dense cytoplasm and no large vacuole.

questions.stem_md: Distinguish between an apical meristem and a lateral meristem on their position and the kind of growth each causes.

answer.model_answer_md: An **apical meristem** lies at the **tips of roots and shoots** and increases the **length** of the plant. A **lateral meristem** (cambium) lies **along the sides** of stems and roots and increases their **girth**.

questions.solution_md: Tip and length; sides and girth.

questions.stem_md: Name the three kinds of meristem. State where each is found and the effect it has on the plant.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Apical**: tips of roots and shoots; increases **length**.
2. **Intercalary**: base of leaves or internodes, as in grasses; increases length at the nodes.
3. **Lateral**: sides of stems and roots (cambium); increases **girth**.

questions.solution_md: Apical, intercalary, lateral with positions and effects.

questions.stem_md: Tough, long fibres from a coconut husk are used to make doormats. The fibres are made of
questions.solution_md: Dead, thick-walled sclerenchyma fibres give strength — option (d).

questions.stem_md: The cells of a potato tuber are living and thin-walled, with small gaps between them, and they are packed with starch. The tissue is
questions.solution_md: Thin-walled living cells with spaces that store food are parenchyma — option (a).

questions.stem_md: A young stem bends in the wind but does not snap. The tissue below its epidermis that allows this has living cells with

options.text_md: walls thickened all round with lignin
a large central nucleus and no cytoplasm

questions.solution_md: Collenchyma gives flexible support through corner thickening — option (a).

questions.stem_md: The parenchyma of a leaf that contains chloroplasts and makes food is called
questions.solution_md: Green parenchyma is chlorenchyma — option (a).

questions.stem_md: A ring of bark including the phloem is cut away from a branch. After some weeks the region just above the cut swells. The swelling is due to

options.text_md: food from the leaves collecting above the cut
water from the roots collecting above the cut

questions.solution_md: Phloem carries food down from the leaves; with it cut, food piles up above the ring — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Which part of the xylem is made of living cells?
questions.solution_md: Only the xylem parenchyma is living — option (c).

questions.stem_md: A sieve tube element has no nucleus, yet it stays alive and works. This is possible because

options.text_md: the nucleus of the neighbouring companion cell controls it
it receives water from the xylem vessels only
its end walls are completely closed

questions.solution_md: The companion cell, with its nucleus, controls the sieve tube — option (b).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Sclerenchyma tissue gives strength and hardness to plant parts.

**Reason (R):** The walls of sclerenchyma cells are thickened with lignin.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and the lignified walls are why the tissue is strong and hard — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Sieve tubes of the phloem are living cells.

**Reason (R):** Sieve tubes have a prominent nucleus.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is true. The reason is false: sieve tubes have no nucleus; the companion cell has one — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Vessels of the xylem carry water upwards efficiently.

**Reason (R):** Vessels are long tubes of dead cells joined end to end without cross-walls.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and the continuous hollow tube is why water moves efficiently — option (c).

questions.stem_md: True or false? Xylem conducts water and minerals from the roots to the leaves.
questions.solution_md: True. Xylem carries water and minerals upwards.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Xylem, Sclerenchyma.

answer.model_answer_md: **Xylem**; the others are **simple permanent tissues**.

questions.solution_md: Xylem is a complex tissue.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Tracheid, Vessel, Sieve tube, Xylem fibre.

answer.model_answer_md: **Sieve tube**; the others are **components of xylem**.

questions.solution_md: The sieve tube is part of phloem.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: sclerenchyma cells are dead when mature.

answer.model_answer_md: Their walls are thickened with **lignin**, which blocks the passage of water and food into the cell, so the **cytoplasm dies**.

questions.solution_md: Lignin blocks entry of materials.

questions.stem_md: The wide, dead tubes of the xylem that carry water are called ______.
questions.solution_md: Vessels.

questions.stem_md: Distinguish between collenchyma and sclerenchyma on the nature of the cells and the thickening of the wall.

answer.model_answer_md: **Collenchyma** cells are **living**, with walls thickened only at the **corners**. **Sclerenchyma** cells are **dead**, with walls thickened all round with **lignin**, leaving a very narrow cavity.

questions.solution_md: Living and corners; dead and lignin.

questions.stem_md: State the part played by the sieve tubes and by the companion cells in the phloem.

answer.model_answer_md: **Sieve tubes** are living tubes that **conduct food** from the leaves to other parts. **Companion cells** lie beside them and, having a **nucleus**, **control** the working of the sieve tubes, which have none.

questions.solution_md: Sieve tubes carry food; companion cells control.

questions.stem_md: Describe the structure of parenchyma and state two of its functions.

answer.model_answer_md: Parenchyma is made of **living**, rounded cells with **thin cellulose walls** and **gaps** between them. Its functions include **storage** of food and water, and **photosynthesis** in green parts such as leaves (chlorenchyma).

questions.solution_md: Living, thin-walled, spaces; storage; photosynthesis.

questions.stem_md: Tabulate three differences between xylem and phloem.

answer.model_answer_md:
| Xylem | Phloem |
|---|---|
| Carries **water and minerals** | Carries **food** |
| Conducts **upwards** | Conducts **up and down** |
| Has **vessels** and tracheids (dead) | Has **sieve tubes** (living) and companion cells |
| Mostly **dead** cells | Mostly **living** cells |

questions.solution_md: Substance, direction, components, living or dead.

questions.stem_md: Red ink rises 24 cm in 40 minutes along a stalk. At what speed does it rise, in cm per hour?
questions.solution_md: 24 cm in 40 min; in 60 min: $24 \div 40 \times 60 = 36$ cm per hour.

questions.stem_md: A stem section has 40 vascular bundles. Each carries 6 sieve tubes. How many sieve tubes are there in all?
questions.solution_md: $40 \times 6 = 240$ sieve tubes.

questions.stem_md: A heavy smoker's windpipe loses the cilia of its lining cells. Which job is most affected?

options.text_md: Sweeping mucus and dust out of the air passage

questions.solution_md: Ciliated epithelium moves mucus and dust upwards — option (c).

questions.stem_md: A strong, slightly elastic band holds the thigh bone to the shin bone at the knee. It is a
questions.solution_md: A ligament joins bone to bone — option (a).

questions.stem_md: The hardness of bone tissue is mainly due to
questions.solution_md: The matrix of bone contains calcium salts — option (a).

questions.stem_md: A section through the lining of the small intestine shows tall, closely packed cells with their nuclei near the base. The epithelium is
questions.solution_md: Tall cells with basal nuclei form columnar epithelium — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Blood is classed as a connective tissue because

options.text_md: its cells lie in a fluid matrix and it links distant parts of the body
it has no cells at all

questions.solution_md: Blood has cells in a fluid matrix (plasma) and connects the body by transport — option (b).

**Assertion (A):** The air sacs of the lungs are lined by squamous epithelium.

**Reason (R):** The windpipe is lined by ciliated epithelium.

Choose the correct option.

questions.stem_md: Explain how the structure of xylem vessels suits their function.

answer.model_answer_md: Vessels are **long, hollow tubes** of **dead** cells joined end to end with **no cross-walls**, so water flows through easily. Their **thick, lignified walls** also stop them collapsing under the pull of water.

questions.stem_md:
A forester drives a nail into a young teak sapling at a height of 1.5 m above the ground. Nine years later the sapling is a tree whose trunk is much thicker, but the nail is still at 1.5 m. A cut across the trunk shows 9 rings of new wood, each 0.4 cm wide.

(a) Explain why the nail stayed at the same height although the tree grew taller. [2]

(b) Name the tissue that thickened the trunk. Calculate the thickness of wood added by the 9 rings. [3]

(c) State one function of collenchyma and one of sclerenchyma in a young stem. [2]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a young plant showing the apical meristem of the shoot, the apical meristem of the root and the lateral meristem. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** The tree grew taller only at its **tip**, by the **apical meristem**; the part of the trunk already formed does not lengthen, so the nail, fixed in older tissue, stays at the same height.

**(b)** The **cambium** (lateral meristem). Thickness = 9 × 0.4 = **3.6 cm**.

**(c)** **Collenchyma** gives **flexible support** to the young stem; **sclerenchyma** gives **strength and hardness**.

**(d)** A plant with a shoot above and a root below the soil; the **shoot-tip** and **root-tip** marked as apical meristems and the **cambium** marked along the stem as the lateral meristem. Three labels with ruled lines.

questions.solution_md: Apical growth at the tip; cambium; 3.6 cm; collenchyma flexible, sclerenchyma strong; labelled plant.

marking_scheme.step: Plant drawn with shoot and root

questions.stem_md:
A student stands a fresh celery stalk in red ink. After 40 minutes the colour has climbed 24 cm up the stalk. She then cuts the stalk across and sees red dots in a ring near the outer edge.

(a) Calculate the speed of the ink in cm per hour. [2]

(b) Name the tissue that carried the ink and state two parts that make it up. [2]

(c) State two features that make this tissue suitable for carrying water. [3]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled diagram of the long section of the tissue that carries food, naming the sieve tube, sieve plate and companion cell. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** 24 cm in 40 min; in 60 min: 24 ÷ 40 × 60 = **36 cm per hour**.

**(b)** **Xylem**; made of **vessels, tracheids**, xylem fibres and xylem parenchyma (any two).

**(c)** Vessels are **long hollow tubes** with **no cross-walls**; the cells are **dead**, so there is no cytoplasm to block the flow; **thick lignified walls** keep the tubes from collapsing. (any two features; third mark for a correct reason)

**(d)** A column of **sieve tube** cells joined end to end, with a **sieve plate** at each joint and a **companion cell** with a nucleus beside each. Three labels.

questions.solution_md: 36 cm per hour; xylem with vessels and tracheids; hollow dead tubes; labelled phloem.

marking_scheme.step: Sieve tubes with sieve plates and companion cells drawn

(a) Name the type of epithelium on each slide. [2]

(b) State the function of the projections on slide P and say what would happen if they were damaged. [3]

(c) Explain why the cells on slide Q are suited to the lung air sac. [2]

**(b)** The **cilia** beat and **sweep mucus with dust and germs** upwards and out of the air passage. If damaged, the mucus would **collect in the lungs**, so dust and germs would not be removed and infection would be more likely.

**(c)** The cells are **thin and flat**, so oxygen and carbon dioxide **diffuse** across them very quickly.

**(d)** A row of **tall cells** standing on a **basement layer**, each with a **nucleus** near the base and **cilia** on the free surface. Three labels.

A student studies three prepared slides. On slide X, 18 of the 50 cells counted show stripes. Slide Y shows striped cells that are branched and joined by dark lines. Slide Z shows spindle-shaped cells with one nucleus each and no stripes.

(a) What percentage of the cells counted on slide X are striped? [2]

(b) Name the muscle on slide Y and give two reasons for your answer. [3]

(c) State where the muscle on slide Z is found and whether it is voluntary or involuntary. [1]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a cell of the muscle on slide Z, naming the cell membrane, nucleus and cytoplasm. [4]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** 18 ÷ 50 × 100 = **36 percent**.

**(b)** **Cardiac muscle**: its cells are **striped and branched**, and are joined by **intercalated discs**, as in the wall of the heart. (any two reasons)

**(c)** In the **wall of the gut** (or blood vessels); **involuntary**.

**(d)** A **spindle-shaped** cell, tapering at both ends, with a **nucleus** in the middle, **cytoplasm** and **cell membrane** labelled; no stripes drawn.

questions.solution_md: 36 percent; cardiac muscle; smooth muscle in gut, involuntary; labelled spindle cell.

questions.stem_md:
A girl touches a hot pan and pulls her hand away at once. The impulse travels along the axon of a neuron, which is 1.2 m long, at 100 m per second.

(a) State, in order, the parts of the neuron that the impulse passes through, starting where it is received. [3]

(b) Calculate the time taken, in milliseconds, for the impulse to travel along this axon. [2]

(c) Name the type of muscle that moves her arm and state whether it is voluntary or involuntary. [1]

(d) Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a neuron, naming five parts. [4]

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** **Dendrites** (receive) → **cell body** (with nucleus) → **axon** → **axon terminals** (pass the impulse on).

**(b)** Time = 1.2 ÷ 100 = 0.012 s = **12 milliseconds**.

**(c)** **Striated (skeletal) muscle**; **voluntary**.

**(d)** A **cell body** with **nucleus**; branched **dendrites**; a long **axon** with myelin sheath; **axon terminals**. Five labels.

questions.solution_md: Dendrites, cell body, axon, terminals; 12 ms; striated voluntary muscle; labelled neuron.

marking_scheme.step: Neuron outline with cell body and dendrites
